title: Use of Typeform Indicators to Show Words in Shapes

illustrates.quote: A transcriber’s note and/or a list of special symbols explains this usage. Sample: In the sentences below, some words are enclosed in a rectangle or an oval. When multiple words are within one shape, a passage indicator rather than a word indicator is used. Symbols used: .=@#7 Words enclosed in a rectangle .=@#' Rectangle terminator .=^#1 Word enclosed in an oval

blocks.features: Braille-only transcriber's note restating rule 5.9.2's own printed symbols legend (rectangle passage indicator/terminator, oval word indicator); no counterpart in this example's own print box.

blocks.text: Boston can be {{td1: very hot}} during the {{td2: summer}} months.
blocks.features: Plain sentence with two enclosing shapes: 'very hot' is boxed in a rectangle outline, and 'summer' is enclosed in an oval outline.

print.notes: Single-sentence example; no heading. The braille carries a transcriber's note restating rule 5.9.2's own printed symbols legend, not part of this example's own print box.
print.surroundingText: Follows rule 5.9.2 and its printed 'Sample:' text directly, on printed page 5-13.
print.printFeatures: Boxed single sentence with a rectangle drawn around 'very hot' and an oval drawn around 'summer'.

braille.notes: Twelve lines, margin 7 stripped (one cell narrower than most others in the section). Lines 1-9 are a transcriber's note ('@.<' ... '@.>') explaining the shapes convention and listing the two symbols — 'words enclosed in a rectangle' passage indicator ('@#7')/terminator ('@#''), and 'word enclosed in an oval' word indicator ('^#1') — with no printed counterpart in the example's own picture box (lines 1-4 have a genuine 4-cell runover indent). Lines 11-12 are the actual sentence: 'very hot' is wrapped in the rectangle passage indicator/terminator pair, and 'summer' carries the oval word indicator immediately before it (no separate terminator, since it is applied to only one word at a time).

resolution: Both runs agree on braille byte-for-byte once run B's leading-indentation-stripping bug is corrected (lines 2-4, 7-8, 11 all lost their genuine runover/list indent in run B). `illustrates.rule` disagreement (A: 5.9.1, B: 5.9.2) resolved in favor of 5.9.2: this rule's own 'Sample:' text is the direct printed source of the exact two-symbol legend (rectangle indicator/terminator, oval indicator) reused verbatim in Example 5-17's own transcriber's note, whereas 5.9.1 is the general statement that a transcriber-defined indicator should be used at all.
